## The task

Have a model produce a three-level WBS for the conference brief. Then write Python (Colab is fine) that checks it mechanically: do children sum to parents, is every element a deliverable noun, are any two siblings overlapping, is the 100% rule satisfied?

**Deliverable.** The WBS, your checking code, its output, and the omissions it caught. The near-universal omissions are project-management labour, contingency, post-event work, and sponsor management — did the model include them? Did your code notice?

## Tutor prompt for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after.

```text
Be my tutor on scope management and work breakdown structures. One question
at a time. Find the gap. I want to be tested specifically on the 100% rule
and on whether I can explain scope creep as a control-system failure rather
than as a discipline problem.
```

## The weekly loop

This lab is step 4–6 of the loop. The whole cycle:

```text
1. TUTOR (diagnostic)  — 10 min — what do I already wrongly believe?
2. Read the module     — 20 min — notes + one primary source
3. TUTOR (voice)       — 20 min — one question at a time, no lecturing
4. Write something     — 15 min — a plan, an argument, a worked problem
5. EDITOR              — 10 min — attack what I wrote
6. ROOMMATE            —  5 min — where else does this structure appear?
7. TUTOR (retrieval)   —  5 min — mixed questions from all prior weeks
```

Steps 4 and 5 do the work. A loop that stops after step 3 feels productive and mostly isn't.

## Submission

Upload to Blackboard as a single PDF. Include your prompts. Label every AI-produced element and attach the verification, per the [AI policy](../syllabus.qmd#artificial-intelligence-policy).
